Manifesto

What we stand for

The drops

Latest drop

The History They Deleted

PA schoolbooks call every non-Muslim ruler an “occupier” and every Muslim conquest a “liberation.” The older editions still mentioned the Jewish kingdoms. The current ones deleted them. Europe funds the system.

Read the piece →

The Week the Bots Went Quiet

Ukraine knocked out three Yandex data centers — and bot-driven “Free Palestine” content fell off a cliff. The Kremlin doesn't care about Palestine. It amplifies everything divisive. Its instruments never knew.

The Bodies Came Back

Israel returned ~400 Palestinian bodies to Gaza. The 91 identified: fighting-age men who died on October 7th, a quarter eulogized as “martyrs” by Hamas itself — all on the Health Ministry's casualty list. A follow-up to Hamas's Own Numbers.

The Palestinians They Don’t March For

Amin Abed — the Gazan dissident Hamas beat with hammers — has a program: disarm Hamas, deradicalize the young, melt the weapons into garbage containers. The movement that claims to care about Palestinians has never heard his name.

The List-Keeper

BBC Arabic's list of “journalists” killed in Gaza — the one found to include Hamas operatives — was compiled by Layla Bashar al-Kloub. Her decade of social media posts calls the killers of Jews “martyrs.” The British Council gave her an award.

The Flags of Sweida

In southern Syria, the Druze — massacred in July 2025, abandoned by Damascus — held an October 7th memorial with Israeli flags and photographs of Netanyahu. Their spiritual leader calls them “an integral part of Israel.”

The Fatwa

Al-Azhar is the oldest and most authoritative institution in Sunni Islam — a thousand years old, half a million students, the Vatican's dialogue partner. On October 7th it saluted the massacre “with absolute pride.” Eleven days later, it issued a religious ruling: there are no innocent Israelis.

The Other Anniversary

On the morning of October 7th, Turkey's state broadcaster aired a highlight reel of Hamas's attack — Quranic verses about victory over footage of the breached Gaza fence. No victims. One day earlier, in Paris, three names were carved into stone.

An Allée in Paris

On Tuesday, the city of Paris inaugurated a park alley bearing the names of Shiri, Ariel and Kfir Bibas — the first permanent tribute to the family anywhere in Europe's public space. Three years after October 7th, their names are now written into the map of Paris.

The Press Files

The IDF published a database of 170 dead "journalists" — with their terror-group ID numbers. Days earlier, the Committee to Protect Journalists had quietly deleted 19 names from its own casualty list. Who was counting?

Death for a Deleted Comment

Sivarasa Anojan, 24, deleted his Facebook comment and filmed an apology. A Saudi court gave him five years and an $800,000 fine. The prosecution appealed — and the sentence became death.

Hamas's Own Numbers

Gaza's health ministry published full 2025 mortality data — natural deaths included, for the first time since the war began. Its own ledger undercuts two of the war's loudest claims.

Waiting on Hamas

Brett McGurk was Biden's negotiator in every hostage round for fifteen months. His on-the-record account of why every deal collapsed.

The Photos Were From February

Angelina Jolie showed the world Gaza from space — nearly a million likes in eleven hours. The images were taken in February.

Zionism Is Racism: Examining the Claim

The Green Party of England and Wales just made it policy — 1,022 to 813. We checked each argument against the historical record.

The jersey nobody's showing you

Zach Bryan wore a "Free Palestine" shirt at Gillette Stadium. Everyone covered the shirt. Nobody showed you the drummer's jersey.
